hooks.title: 800 MILES OF LINES

hooks.title: FROM 500 BC

hooks.text: Lines and animals cover about fifty square kilometers of this desert in Peru.
hooks.title: 50 SQUARE KM

beats.text: Who scratched over eight hundred miles of lines into this desert?
They're only inches deep. How have they lasted?
This century, drones found several hundred new figures.
Most run straight. Others draw animals, like the one known as the Monkey.
Together they cover about seven thousand football pitches of ground.
Over fifteen hundred years ago, people lifted off the reddish-brown surface pebbles.
That bared the yellow-grey ground underneath, and the lines appeared.
Dry, windless, stable weather has preserved them ever since.
Next target: a Nevada base where all research is classified. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

draft.description: The Nazca lines are geoglyphs in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru, made between 500 BC and 500 AD by removing reddish-brown pebbles to expose lighter subsoil. Their combined length is more than 1,300 km, and drones have found several hundred new figures this century.
